shouldFix.title: The new ustar tail specification states the chksum computation rule incorrectly against POSIX ustar, and gives devmajor/devminor two incompatible encodings
detail: CHECKSUM. metadata.checksum reads: 'POSIX ustar chksum: sum of header bytes with the checksum field treated as six spaces plus one space and one NUL (six octal digits, then NUL, then space). Stored as six octal digits, NUL, space.' The stored layout is right - six octal digits, NUL, space is the conventional ustar encoding. The computation rule is not. POSIX ustar computes the checksum over the 512-byte header with all EIGHT chksum octets taken as ASCII space (0x20). v5 instructs that the field be treated as six spaces plus one space and one NUL, i.e. seven spaces and one NUL.

The consequence is arithmetic and exact: a NUL contributes 0 where a space contributes 0x20, so every header written to this rule carries a chksum value 32 lower than the value any conforming reader recomputes. Every member header therefore fails checksum verification in standard tar, and the archive is not a valid POSIX ustar stream even though /archiveProfile/encoding declares 'POSIX ustar (ustar\0)'.

The error looks like the stored layout was reused as the computation mask: substituting spaces for the six octal digits of '000000\0 ' yields the '(six spaces) + NUL + space' shape the text describes, instead of the all-spaces mask the format requires.

DEVMAJOR/DEVMINOR. metadata.devmajor and metadata.devminor both read 'empty / zero. Not used (no devices).' Empty and zero are different bytes: an empty field is NUL or space fill, a zero field is octal ASCII '0000000' plus NUL. The sibling metadata.numericFields resolves it one way - it lists devmajor and devminor among fields that are 'octal ASCII, leading zeros, NUL-terminated' - so the two clauses in the same block disagree, and the 'empty /' alternative admits bytes numericFields forbids.

I record what v5 got right, because it is most of the finding I raised. linkname is now 'exactly TreeCommitment.target' for symlinks and empty otherwise, which is the datum schemas.v11's treeCommitmentShape supplies and the gap that left symlink trees undetermined. The trailer is now 'Exactly two 512-byte zero blocks after the last member. No further padding', which closes the blocking-factor divergence between POSIX-minimum and GNU-default writers and makes archive length a function of the member set. size is fixed for files, dirs and symlinks. numericFields names the octal/NUL convention. That is the substance of CLAUDE-V4-S2.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: archiveProfile.standing claims 'Closed profile opensip-archive-profile.1' and encoding declares POSIX ustar; CI-3 rides byte-identity on the profile and CI-5 now pins the token as a CI input. A profile that is precise but non-conforming produces archives that no standard reader accepts, which matters directly at OC-7, where the archive bytes are an air-gap install input. The devmajor/devminor ambiguity is smaller but is the same species of gap the last two rounds have been closing.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Internal determinism survives: two adapters following v5 literally emit identical bytes, so CI-3's same-archiveDigest promise still holds and nothing unsafe is authorized. The defect is conformance to the declared format plus one internal contradiction, and both are single-clause fixes.
shouldFix.remedy: State the computation as 'the eight chksum octets are taken as ASCII space (0x20) when summing; the stored value is six octal digits, NUL, space.' Delete the 'empty /' alternative from devmajor and devminor so numericFields governs, or state the exact byte fill if empty is intended.
